summary.intent: Plan Phase 51 (IPNS crypto-signature hardening) in parallel with discussing Phase 52 (Desktop FUSE durability), with Phase 51 planning isolated in a dedicated git worktree to avoid branch-switching collisions.
summary.outcome: Phase 51 planner was isolated to a dedicated worktree (`cipher-box-p51`) and restarted after a session limit interruption; Phase 52 CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md were written and committed to `feat/desktop-fuse-durability-at-rest-safety`, branched cleanly from `main`.

repo: GSD commit helper auto-switches the working tree branch on first phase commit (main → feat/<slug>), which conflicts with background agents running in the same tree targeting a different phase.
The repo uses `core.hooksPath` pointing to an absolute path in the main worktree's `.husky`, so all worktrees share the same pre-commit hook and require `node_modules` to run lint-staged.
Todo files live under `.planning/todos/pending/` — a stale reference in 51-CONTEXT.md pointed to the wrong path.
Phase 51 scope was locked to S1/S2/S3 IPNS crypto-signature work after todo #15 (logger redaction + Faro) was deferred to a future observability phase.

Phase 52 covers FUSE write-journal hardening (HARD-03) including IN-04 (sanitize_error scrub list extension) and IN-05 (log::warn! on swallowed journal.remove() errors), touching shared `crates/sdk` + `crates/fuse`.
workflow: Background agents on this harness DO support nesting sub-agents (Tools: * includes the Agent tool), making the manager workflow's conservative 'no nesting in background' guardrail stale.

Launching a background agent without `isolation: 'worktree'` in a repo that auto-switches branches on phase commits creates a real collision risk — always use worktree isolation for parallel phase work.
Symlinking node_modules into a worktree is fragile; `pnpm i` in the worktree is the correct approach for proper isolated deps.
A session limit mid-agent leaves the worktree in a recoverable state as long as no commits were made — verify git status before restarting.

The plan-phase pipeline requires: researcher → pattern-mapper → planner → independent plan-checker; collapsing to a single agent (as happens without proper sub-agent support) is a meaningful quality regression.

friction: Session limit interrupted the Phase 51 planner mid-execution, requiring a full restart.
Background agent was initially launched without worktree isolation, requiring a stop-and-restart cycle with manual worktree setup.
The manager workflow's 'no nesting in background' guardrail was stale/wrong for this harness, causing an initial incorrect refusal to run the plan pipeline in the background.
The stale todo path reference in 51-CONTEXT.md (discovered by the stopped planner) was tricky to fix cleanly due to husky hooks requiring node_modules in the worktree.
The worktree had no node_modules initially, blocking any commits via the pre-commit hook until pnpm i was run.
